title: Node context inspection
description: Objective: make node input, result, context, and recovery identities visibly distinct without turning missing proof into success. Deliverable: apps/control-room/src/nodes/node-context.tsx and node-context.test.tsx, a presentation-only React section over explicit daemon-projected/preclassified props. It must separately label started graph revision/binding, input binding hash, input manifest/tree digests, result manifest/tree digests, contextDigest, providerInputDigest, token/byte coverage, and recovery state/reason/allowed commands. NOT in scope: context selection, digest calculation, provider tokenization, recovery-policy inference, fetching, routing/mounting, receipts/artifacts, or edits outside the two files. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/control-room exec vitest run src/nodes/node-context.test.tsx.
definitionOfDone: Focused tests assert input binding, input manifest/tree, result manifest/tree, context, and provider-input identities have separate accessible labels and cannot collapse into one generic hash.
Recovery state, reason, and allowed commands are rendered only as supplied daemon facts; no client-side recovery or readiness inference exists.
Missing digest, tokenization, or proof metadata renders UNKNOWN with provenance and never zero, verified, current, or successful wording.
node-context.tsx and node-context.test.tsx are each <=250 physical lines and the exact focused verification command exits 0.
taskRails: Accept already-projected presentation props only; do not define an authoritative wire schema or calculate hashes/currentness in the UI.
Keep context used by workers distinct from the clean review graph/plan context and preserve UNKNOWN for missing token/proof measurements.
Own and stage only apps/control-room/src/nodes/node-context.tsx and node-context.test.tsx.
